## Investigación con agentes (Claude Opus 5.5; puede contener errores)
# Research notes: will the DFB formally come out against Infantino's FIFA presidency before Oct 16, 2026? (compiled 2026-10-05)

As of Oct 5, 2026 there is no qualifying statement. No DFB press release or Präsidium resolution says the DFB will not back Infantino's re-election, has lost confidence in him, or wants him to step down. Every strong anti-Infantino line so far comes from Neuendorf or Watzke personally. The only institutional act is not signing his letter of support, which the fine print says does not count on its own.

## 1. What the resolution source shows (dfb.de/news)
- **dfb.de/news front page, checked 2026-10-05:** sports items only, nothing on Infantino, FIFA or the Präsidium.
  - *Uncertain:* there was no full-text search of dfb.de, so a very recent item may be missing from search indexes.
- **2026-05-01, official dfb.de item** ([link](https://www.dfb.de/news/neuendorf-statement-zu-erneuter-infantino-kandidatur)): the DFB took no position on Infantino's candidacy.
  - Neuendorf said judging it "is not my sole decision, but falls to our governing bodies" ("obliegt unseren Gremien").
  - The DFB will examine the candidacy together with the DFL (the German league body) and decide "after the application deadline closes".
  - That deadline is Nov 18, 2026, which is after this question closes.
- **2026-08-01, dfb.de** ([link](https://www.dfb.de/news/this-step-was-inevitable-neuendorf-welcomes-fifas-decision-to-drop-investor-plans)): about FIFA dropping its investor plans. Quote: "The FIFA president acted unilaterally and without transparency…". This is criticism only and takes none of positions (a), (b) or (c).
- **2026-09-11, dfb.de** ([link](https://www.dfb.de/news/regionalliga-reform-dfb-praesidium-bereitet-ausserordentlichen-bundestag-vor)): the Präsidium met and called an extraordinary DFB Bundestag (general assembly) for Dec 18, 2026. Nothing on FIFA.
- **Precedent, before the question opened (2023-03-15)** ([dfb.de](https://www.dfb.de/news/detail/neuendorf-dfb-unterstuetzt-wiederwahl-von-infantino-nicht-249330)): "Der DFB wird die Wiederwahl von FIFA-Präsident Gianni Infantino in Kigali nicht unterstützen."
  - This was published on dfb.de, worded as an organisational position and attributed to Neuendorf.
  - It concerns the 2023 Kigali election, not March 2027, so it does not satisfy (a). It does show the DFB has issued exactly this kind of statement before.

## 2. Recent news and current situation
- **2026-04-30:** Infantino announced his candidacy. Reports say more than 200 of FIFA's 211 associations signed his support letter.
- **2026-07-15:** the DFB confirmed to the German press agency SID that it had not signed the support letter: "Der DFB hat kein Unterstützungsschreiben … unterschrieben". It added: "Weitere Schritte werden im DFB-Präsidium beraten" ("further steps will be discussed in the Präsidium").
  - Sources: [ZDF](https://www.zdfheute.de/sport/fussball-wm/wm-fifa-neuendorf-dfb-neuendorf-wiederwahl-100.html), [Goal](https://www.goal.com/en-us/lists/german-fa-refuses-endorse-gianni-infantino-re-election-fifa-president-amid-growing-scrutiny/bltb30b9c9dddb32e15).
  - This was a spokesperson statement to media, which counts only as non-endorsement.
- **2026-09-09:** Neuendorf said FIFA must be "grundlegend und umfassend reformiert" and promised "weitere Wegmarken" (further milestones) ([Sport1](https://www.sport1.de/news/fussball/2026/09/infantino-neuendorf-kuendigt-weitere-wegmarken-an)).
- **2026-09-15, Thessaloniki:** Neuendorf said the trust with Infantino is "natürlich zerrüttet" (naturally broken) and that ending the "System Infantino" is "zwingend erforderlich" (imperative). He promised "important decisions" at the Berlin meeting.
  - Sportschau says explicitly that this is **not** a formal Präsidium decision ([Sportschau](https://www.sportschau.de/fussball/neuendorf-system-infantino-muss-beendet-werden,neuendorf-infantino-102.html), [kicker](https://www.kicker.de/neuendorf-system-infantino-muss-beendet-werden-1253008/artikel)).
- **2026-09-17:** Watzke said "Er sollte weg, ohne Wenn und Aber" ("He should go, no ifs or buts"). He was speaking personally ([Sport1](https://www.sport1.de/news/fussball/2026/09/er-sollte-weg-watzke-stellt-sich-gegen-infantino)).
- **2026-09-21 to 09-24:** Infantino sent a reform letter to all 211 associations. Neuendorf called it a "durchschaubares Manöver" (transparent manoeuvre) and said Infantino had forfeited all credibility. Personal remarks again ([Sportschau](https://www.sportschau.de/fussball/neuendorf-nennt-infantino-angebot-durchschaubares-manoever,neuendorf-infantino-brief-100.html)).
- **Outlets saying the DFB has not formally withdrawn support:**
  - [Feverpitch](https://www.feverpitch.de/infantino-kauft-sich-mit-einem-reformbrief-zeit-der-dfb-darf-sie-ihm-nicht-schenken/), 2026-09-22.
  - [SRF](https://www.srf.ch/sport/fussball/fussball-allgemein/sfv-einer-von-vielen-verbaenden-wer-hat-sich-bisher-von-infantino-abgewendet), 2026-10-01.
  - time.news, dated around 2026-10-05.
  - Feverpitch notes a conflict for Neuendorf: he is also a FIFA Council member.
  - One English summary quotes the DFB as saying there was "no basis to withdraw support… given there was no support to begin with". The source and date are unverified.
- **Other associations (formal withdrawals, per [Wikipedia, 77th FIFA Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/77th_FIFA_Congress)):**
  - Jul 30 to Aug 3: Finland, Wales, Serbia, Sweden.
  - Aug 4 to Aug 26: Greece, England, Norway, Ireland, New Zealand, Gibraltar, Northern Ireland, Italy.
  - By mid-September: France and Austria.
  - Around Sep 30 / Oct 1: Switzerland ([kicker](https://www.kicker.de/schweiz-entzieht-infantino-unterstuetzung-fuer-weitere-fifa-amtszeit-1257326/artikel)).
  - Norway (Aug 7–11) called for Infantino to resign, reportedly after its board met ([The Standard](https://www.thestandard.com.hk/football/article/339553/Norway-FA-president-Klaveness-calls-on-FIFA-boss-Infantino-to-resign)). The board link is unverified.
  - SRF claims at least 50 associations oppose him, including the USA and Canada. This is unverified and doubtful.
- **UEFA:**
  - Early August: UEFA president Čeferin said FIFA's leadership had lost UEFA's confidence.
  - Around 2026-09-29: Čeferin said "Der Kaiser ist nackt" ("the emperor has no clothes").
  - UEFA is looking for a rival candidate but had none as of Sep 29 ([Sportschau](https://www.sportschau.de/fussball/lange-suche-nach-einem-gegenkandidaten-fuer-infantino,efc-generalversammlung-kopenhagen-fifa-100.html)).
- **Rival candidates:** none declared. CONCACAF president Montagliani is mentioned most often.
- **Overall vote count:** on 2026-09-10 Reuters reported, via [TSN](https://www.tsn.ca/soccer/article/report-embattled-infantino-still-on-course-for-re-election/), that Infantino still has majority support, mainly in Africa, Asia and South America.

### Scheduled events before Oct 16
- **Oct 8–9, Berlin:** meeting of presidents and general secretaries of all 55 UEFA associations, hosted by the DFB. Neuendorf has tied "important decisions" to it, so it is the most likely trigger for any formal DFB step.
  - *Uncertain:* a time.news piece dated Oct 5 suggests the meeting may already be under way.
- **Oct 15, Zurich:** FIFA Council meeting on governance and reform. Neuendorf is a member.
- **No DFB Präsidium meeting is publicly scheduled before Oct 16.** Präsidium dates are usually not announced in advance.
- **Later dates, after the question closes:** Nov 18, 2026 nomination deadline (a candidate needs 5 nominating associations); Dec 18, 2026 DFB Bundestag; Mar 18, 2027 FIFA Congress in Rabat.

### Prediction markets
None covers the DFB specifically.
- **Kalshi, "Infantino out as FIFA president this year":** 40% on 2026-08-04 ([Kalshi](https://news.kalshi.com/p/gianni-infantino-fifa-exit-odds)). Volume unknown.
- **Polymarket, Infantino out by Dec 31:** about 36.5%, reported by [BeInCrypto](https://beincrypto.com/infantino-trump-favor-polymarket-exit-odds/), probably in August. Date and volume unverified.

## 3. Base rates
- **2015, Blatter:** the DFB moved with the UEFA bloc behind Prince Ali. No separate formal DFB resolution was found (uncertain). In October 2015, after Blatter's suspension and announced exit, DFB president Niersbach personally said the future must be "ohne Sepp Blatter" ([Sport1](https://www.sport1.de/internationaler-fussball/2015/10/fifa-skandal-dfb-praesident-wolfgang-niersbach-fordert-blatter-ruecktritt)).
- **2019:** then-DFB president Grindel set conditions (Feb 2019). After he resigned, the DFB executive board voted unanimously to back Infantino, who was acclaimed on Jun 5, 2019.
- **2022:** around Nov 17, 2022, Inside World Football reported that the DFB would not back Infantino's re-election ([link](https://www.insideworldfootball.com/2022/11/17/germans-wont-support-infantinos-re-election-calling-concrete-action-human-rights/)).
- **2023:** formal non-support on dfb.de (Mar 15), quoted in section 1. It did not call for him to resign, and Infantino was acclaimed on Mar 16, 2023.
- **2024–2025, the DFB going along with FIFA:**
  - Dec 2024: an extraordinary DFB board vote unanimously backed the 2030/2034 World Cup awards, including Saudi Arabia 2034 ([kicker](https://www.kicker.de/wm-vergabe-2034-nach-saudi-arabien-dfb-stimmt-mit-ja-1073534/artikel)).
  - Dec 2025: Neuendorf defended FIFA's peace prize for Trump.
- **Pattern:** the DFB tends to withhold support (2023 formally; 2026 so far only by not signing) rather than demand resignations. Its formal decisions usually go through the Präsidium, not Neuendorf alone. Neuendorf has said the 2026–27 decision would come after the Nov 18 deadline, which is later than this question's window.

## Things to watch
- Whether the Oct 8–9 Berlin meeting produces a DFB press release or Präsidium resolution.
- Whether the media start describing Neuendorf's or Watzke's remarks as the official DFB position.
- Whether the DFB sticks to its May 1 line of deciding only after Nov 18.

criterios: This question resolves YES if, before October 16, 2026, the German Football Association (Deutscher Fußball-Bund, DFB) issues an official statement attributed to the DFB as an organisation — such as a DFB press release, an official statement posted to the DFB news portal, or a formally communicated resolution of its Präsidium/presidential board (Präsidialausschuss) — that explicitly commits the DFB to at least one of the following positions regarding Gianni Infantino: (a) that the DFB will not support his re-election as FIFA president at the March 2027 Congress; (b) that the DFB no longer has confidence in, or withdraws its support from, his leadership as FIFA president; or (c) that the DFB calls for him to step down or be replaced as FIFA president. Qualifying wording includes institutional phrasing such as "the DFB will not support Infantino's re-election", "the DFB has lost confidence in" or "no longer supports" Infantino, or "the DFB calls for new leadership at FIFA". The statement must be verifiable via the DFB's official news portal ([dfb.de](https://www.dfb.de/news)) or reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) as an official DFB organisational position. Otherwise the question resolves NO.
letra_pequena: Personal remarks by individual DFB officials speaking in their own name in interviews or press appearances (for example president Bernd Neuendorf or vice-president Hans-Joachim Watzke stating that Infantino "must go" or that his "system must end") do NOT by themselves count, unless they are explicitly presented as, or the reporting explicitly characterises them as, an official position of the DFB as an organisation. Generic criticism of Infantino's conduct or FIFA governance that does not explicitly take one of positions (a), (b), or (c) above does not count. Declining to sign a letter of support (mere non-endorsement), without an accompanying explicit institutional statement taking one of positions (a), (b), or (c), does not by itself count. A qualifying statement issued or adopted at any time before October 16, 2026 counts toward resolution, including one that predates October 15, 2026.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** About 11 days, from October 5 until October 16, 2026.  
(b) **Status quo:** NO. The DFB has not issued a qualifying institutional statement.  
(c) **Reference class:** The DFB formally declined to support Infantino’s 2023 re-election, so it has a precedent for doing this. But that decision came close to the election; there is no reliable base rate for doing so within an 11-day window.  
(d) **NO scenario:** After the October 8–9 UEFA meeting, officials continue their criticism, but the DFB waits until after the November nomination deadline to adopt a formal position.  
(e) **YES scenario:** The meeting prompts a DFB Präsidium decision or official statement explicitly opposing Infantino’s re-election or calling for new FIFA leadership.  
(f) **Resolution technicality:** Not signing a support letter—and even forceful personal remarks by DFB officials—does not count. The opposition must be explicitly attributed to the DFB as an organisation.

The imminent meeting and strong rhetoric make a formal statement plausible. The short deadline and the DFB’s stated intention to decide after November 18 keep NO more likely.

Probability: 38%

**(a) Time left:** About 11 days, from Oct 5 to Oct 16, 2026. The key events in that window are the UEFA associations' meeting in Berlin on Oct 8–9, hosted by the DFB, and the FIFA Council meeting on Oct 15, which Neuendorf attends as a member.

**(b) Status quo:** No. Every strong anti-Infantino line so far comes from Neuendorf or Watzke personally. The DFB's only institutional act is not signing the support letter, which does not count on its own. The DFB's official stated line, on dfb.de in May, is that its governing bodies will decide after the Nov 18 nomination deadline. That is after this window closes.

**(c) Reference class:**
- **Past formal non-support:** the DFB has issued exactly this kind of statement before. It formally declined to back Infantino in 2023 on dfb.de, and reportedly did so in 2022. Both came shortly before the vote or at moments of crisis, not months ahead.
- **Peer federations in 2026:** roughly 15 European federations formally withdrew support over Aug–Oct. That shows there is a cascade and pressure on the DFB.
- **How the DFB decides:** it tends to act through its Präsidium on its own timeline, and Neuendorf has a conflict as a FIFA Council member.
- **Base rate:** for a specific formal statement inside a short 11-day window, without a scheduled Präsidium meeting, the base rate is low, perhaps 15–25%.

**(d) No scenario:** The Berlin meeting ends with UEFA-level talk of strategy or a search for a rival candidate. Neuendorf gives more sharp personal quotes. The DFB keeps to its "we never supported him, we'll decide after Nov 18" line, and the Präsidium takes formal action only later, around November or December.

**(e) Yes scenario:** At or after the Berlin meeting, which Neuendorf tied to "important decisions", the DFB Präsidium adopts a resolution or dfb.de publishes a statement. It could read "Der DFB wird die Wiederwahl … nicht unterstützen", or join a coordinated UEFA declaration calling for new FIFA leadership in 2027. This would most likely come before or just after the Oct 15 Council meeting.

**(f) Technicalities:**
- A dfb.de item quoting Neuendorf in organisational wording would likely count. The 2023 precedent was in exactly that format, which lowers the bar.
- Reporting that calls Neuendorf's remarks "the DFB's position" could also tip the resolution.
- On the other hand, the DFB's "no support to withdraw" framing is pure non-endorsement and does not count.
- A UEFA joint statement that the DFB does not separately adopt would be ambiguous.

The Berlin trigger and the peer cascade give a real chance. The DFB's stated timeline and the absence of any scheduled Präsidium meeting keep the probability well below even.

Probability: 27%
